records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: A paddling club on Ridge Avenue in Philadelphia, founded in 1905. It teaches canoe, kayak and stand-up paddleboard, and its trips, racing and social paddles are open to the public without a membership.
records.what_you_do: Take a lesson in kayak, canoe, paddleboard or pool sessions, then join club trips, social paddles or fall work days.

schedule.text: Trips and training run year round. Listings for October 2026 through January 2027 include monthly club meetings and fall work days. Class times are not on the page.

cost.text: Dues and class fees not stated on the page read

first_step.how: Check the event calendar on the club site, pick a beginner class or trip, and email the club office at admin@philacanoe.org with questions
first_step.basis: Trips and training are open to the public and the club lists a contact address, but class times are not on the page

records.notes: Delaware River trip skill requirements appeared only in a search snippet, so they are not recorded. Membership levels linked from the site were not read.

records.name: Glen Foerd
records.summary: A park and mansion on the Delaware River in Northeast Philadelphia. Its free open boating days let visitors take out a canoe, rowboat or kayak on the creek and the river.
records.what_you_do: Paddle or row on a free open boating day, join a guided birdwatching kayak tour when one is offered, or check the events list for other river programs.

schedule.text: Free open boating days, with no weekday or hours given in the listing. A guided birdwatching kayak tour was dated October 10, 2026 and was marked sold out.

cost.text: Free open boating days, per the events listing

first_step.how: Watch the events listing for the next free open boating day and go during the posted hours, or call 215.632.5330 to ask about sign-up
first_step.basis: Open boating is listed as free and open to visitors; the page gives no age, skill or sign-up rules

records.notes: The open boating listing says this summer but carries an October 24, 2026 date, so its timing is unclear. The site says the park is run by Glen Foerd Conservation Corporation in cooperation with Philadelphia Parks and Recreation. The paddle trips run by Delaware Riverkeeper Network start here.

records.name: Delaware Riverkeeper Network
records.summary: A nonprofit membership group that works to keep the Delaware River clean and free-flowing. It runs free learn-to-paddle trips on the river from Glen Foerd in Northeast Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a free guided paddle on the river, join as a member or volunteer, or follow the group's river campaigns.

schedule.text: Free paddles from Glen Foerd on a daytime schedule. The June 27, 2026 paddle ran 10:30 am to 3 pm. A learn-to-paddle trip in July 2024 ran 4:30 to 7:30 pm.

cost.text: Free, per the June 2026 and July 2024 listings

first_step.how: Use the register link on the group's paddle event page; seats are first come, first served, you sign a waiver, and you should arrive 15 minutes early
first_step.basis: The trips are labeled learn-to-paddle and explain how to register and what to expect on arrival

records.notes: The June 2026 paddle page does not name its organizer; it is listed on the group's own site and calendar. The age rule (ages 14 and up, minors with an adult) comes from the July 2024 listing only, and the 2026 listing gives no age rule. The group's office is in Bristol, Pennsylvania, outside the city. The home page lists no Philadelphia programs of its own.

records.name: Ocean Blue Project
records.summary: A nonprofit based in Virginia that organizes trash cleanups along the Delaware and Schuylkill rivers in Philadelphia, including the Penn's Landing waterfront and Fairmount Park riverbanks.
records.what_you_do: Join a 1 to 2 hour cleanup on a riverbank or green space, with gloves, bags and tools provided, or ask to organize a group cleanup.

schedule.text: Cleanups run through the year and usually last 1 to 2 hours. The page does not list specific Philadelphia dates; those are on its list of river cleanup events.

locations.label: Penn's Landing waterfront and Fairmount Park riverbanks (sites vary)

cost.text: Supplies are provided and a donation is optional

first_step.how: Open the page that lists Philadelphia river cleanups and sign up for a date; groups send a registration form at least 6 weeks ahead
first_step.basis: The page says no prior experience is needed and that families, students and youth groups are welcome

records.notes: The office is in Lottsburg, Virginia, and the Philadelphia cleanups are one of its local programs. Status is probably_active because the site is current (it cites 2026 guides) but the page read gives no dated Philadelphia event. The cleanup pages on the site are the place to check for dates.

records.name: Riverfront North Partnership
records.summary: A nonprofit that looks after the Delaware River Greenway in Northeast Philadelphia. It runs a volunteer program and Learn to Fish days at Pleasant Hill Park, and it lists a Friends of Borski Park program.
records.what_you_do: Ask about volunteer days on the Greenway, join a Learn to Fish day or the summer fishing camp at Pleasant Hill Park, or take part in its environmental education.

schedule.text: The home page shows no written dates for its programs. Ask the office for the current volunteer and fishing schedule.

cost.text: Learn to Fish has free rod and bait rentals, per the page; other costs not stated

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-425-8350 or email info@riverfrontnorth.org to ask about volunteer days, since the volunteer page does not describe how to sign up

records.notes: The only dated volunteer event found was a shoreline cleanup at Pennypack on the Delaware on August 17, 2019, which the listing marks as ended. The home page shows no written dates, so probably_active rests on a working site rather than dated evidence. This is a park and Greenway group, not a boating group; it is recorded for its Delaware riverfront volunteering. Friends of Borski Park is named as a program and was not checked separately.

records.name: Head of the Schuylkill Regatta
records.summary: The volunteer crew behind a large rowing race on the Schuylkill River. Volunteers work the docks, timing, registration, launches, photos, parking and the zero waste team.
records.what_you_do: Pick a half-day shift in timing, docks, parking, registration or another role, or help with the riverbank clean-up before race day.

schedule.text: Shifts are generally half days that break around lunchtime. For the 2026 regatta, registration packets are assembled October 18 and a volunteer information session is held on Zoom on Tuesday, October 20.

cost.text: Volunteering is unpaid; no fee is listed on the page

first_step.how: Use the SignUpGenius link on the volunteer page (it opens after August 1); a captain then contacts you to confirm shifts. Questions go to volunteers@hosr.org
first_step.basis: Timing needs no rowing or timing experience and training is given, and the page explains each step of sign-up

records.notes: Golf cart drivers must be 18 or older with a license, and launch volunteers need outboard boating experience. The page does not give race dates or the course route, so the location is the Schuylkill River named in the regatta's name. The page footer names Thomas Eakins Head of the Schuylkill Regatta, Inc.; nonprofit status is not stated on the page.

records.name: Stotesbury Cup Regatta
records.summary: A spring rowing regatta on the Schuylkill River, run by the Schuylkill Navy of Philadelphia. It needs volunteers for course set-up, registration, race-day docks, launch driving and results.
records.what_you_do: Help set up the course on the Wednesday, staff registration on the Thursday, or help on the docks, with results and vendors on race days. Two or more shifts earn Regatta Enclosure entry passes.

schedule.text: The 99th regatta was May 15 and 16, 2026. Volunteer roles run Wednesday (install crew), Thursday (registration from 2 to 6 pm and practice day) and Friday and Saturday (race day).

cost.text: Volunteering is unpaid; two or more shifts earns entry passes

first_step.how: Fill in the Volunteer on Land form linked from the regatta site, or use the separate sign-up page if you are an experienced launch driver; install crew volunteers email the organizers
first_step.basis: The page says most volunteer jobs need no rowing experience and lists how to sign up for each role

records.notes: The page names the Schuylkill Navy of Philadelphia as organizer; its nonprofit status is not stated on the page read. Experienced launch drivers have a separate sign-up. No minimum age for volunteers is given. The volunteer contact named on the page is a private person and was not recorded.

records.name: Jefferson Dad Vail Regatta
records.notes: The regatta is held on the Cooper River in Pennsauken, New Jersey, at the Camden County Boathouse, so it does not meet in Philadelphia. The volunteer page read covers the 2023 regatta. The home page contradicts itself: a banner says the 2027 regatta is May 7 and 8, while the body text says Friday May 7 and Saturday May 8, 2026. Individual officers' personal contact details on the pages were not recorded. Sources read: https://dadvail.org/ and https://dadvail.org/?p=3010.

leads_only.name: Friends of Pennypack Park
leads_only.note: Named in a 2014 article about its cleanups. The article returned HTTP 403, so no website or current evidence was read. Not checked.

blocked.note: Liberty Sailing Club, which appeared in search results as a Delaware River sailing club open to newcomers. The site returned 403 on the first and only attempt. Not retried and not recorded. A later run with access should check it.
Corinthian Yacht Club of Philadelphia's own site, linked from a SpinSheet page that says it runs adult and junior learn-to-sail programs. Returned 503 on two tries. Not recorded.
2014 article naming the Friends of Pennypack Park cleanups. Blocked, so no group website was found.

notes: Searches: all 3 used (standard mode). Fetches: 24, including two retries of the Corinthian site. Stopped before the fetch budget because the remaining candidates were blocked, out of area, or had no verifiable Philadelphia join path. The brief named no starting list page, so the three searches were the list. Gaps: no Frankford Arsenal or Frankford Creek boat launch group turned up in search, and no current Pennypack paddling program was found (only a 2021 Riverfront North and Glen Foerd outing, not recorded). Paddle Penn's Landing is a 2009 free kayak program with a later $5 version, and no current evidence was found, so it was dropped. Dropped after reading: Delaware River Sojourn (an annual paddle organized by the Delaware River Basin Commission with a steering committee, June 20 to 26, 2026, starting in New York and heading back toward Philadelphia's Pleasant Hill Park; it is an event rather than a group, and no end point or fee is confirmed, so the owner may want it as a calendar entry); Independence Seaport Museum (website https://www.phillyseaport.org/ lists no public boating or volunteer join path; its Sailor STEM program is school-based per a June 2023 news story); Living Lands and Waters (no Philadelphia cleanups on its site, last Philadelphia cleanup evidence August 2015 on the city water blog); Partnership for the Delaware Estuary (Wilmington office, volunteer page, no dated Philadelphia events); Philadelphia Water Department cleanup posts (city government, skipped). Not read, named only in search results: SailTime (commercial membership sailing), Schooner North Wind (charter listing), Union League and Quaker City yacht clubs (membership clubs), Gloucester City Sail (New Jersey), Bartram's Garden boating program (no website link found on a page read), and the Bicycle Coalition's Big Paddle (a 2025 event, cycling lane). Ocean Blue Project's office is in Virginia. Glen Foerd and Delaware Riverkeeper Network both list a June 2026 or October 2026 date, so both are active. Riverfront North is recorded at low confidence because its site shows no written dates.
